vocab.title: Match each expression to its meaning
defs: as a result of this, and in a way that fits it
the reasons behind a decision or a position
the most important point, the one that decides
said in fewer and easier words
what you accept to lose in order to gain something else
in what really happens, not in theory
in spite of what was just said; even so

items.situation: Paulo asks: "Why a fixed price at all?"
tips: Because the buyer needs certainty. Therefore, a fixed price makes the first contract easier to sign.
The reason, then therefore for the result.

items.situation: He asks: "Is that not risky for us?"
tips: Although there is a risk, it is smaller than it looks, because the first sale is small.
although: admit the problem, keep the position.

items.situation: He asks: "What is the difference between their needs and ours?"
tips: They need certainty, whereas we need a buyer who will still be there.

items.situation: He asks: "Anything else that protects us?"
tips: In addition, the price can be reviewed after the first monitoring period.
in addition: one more point, same direction.
On the other hand, if the market falls sharply, we will sell below value.
on the other hand: be fair to the other side.

items.situation: He asks: "Give me the bottom line."
tips: To put it simply: accept the fixed price and keep the review clause.

reading.rtitle: Fixed Price or Floating? A Short Internal Opinion
paras: With regard to the question raised by the finance director, our position is that the company should accept a fixed price for the first sale of credits from the Serra Verde project, but only if the payment is linked to issuance and not to a calendar date.

The rationale is simple. A buyer that approves its budgets a year in advance needs certainty, whereas we need a buyer that will still be there when the credits are issued. A fixed price gives the buyer that certainty. Therefore, it makes the first contract much easier to sign, and at this stage a first contract matters more than a perfect one.

In practice, the price risk is smaller than it looks. The first sale covers two hundred thousand credits, which is less than a fifth of what the project is expected to produce. As a result, even a large fall in the market would affect only a small part of our income. In addition, the draft clause allows the price to be reviewed after the first monitoring period.

Although a fixed price protects the buyer more than it protects us, the trade-off is acceptable. On the other hand, if the market falls sharply before the credits are issued, we will have sold below value, and the board should know that before it approves. Nonetheless, the alternative, a floating price, would probably end the negotiation.

To put it simply: accept the fixed price, link the payment to issuance, and keep the review clause. The bottom line is that the first contract gives the project its first buyer, and we recommend proceeding accordingly.

listenings.text: Amanda, it is Paulo from finance. I read the opinion, and I agree with most of it, so this is not a complaint. It is a request. On Thursday the board will ask me one question, and I already know which one: what happens if the price falls by half before the credits are issued. Please do not give me a one-line answer this time. The last time I said the risk was small and somebody asked why, I had nothing else to say. I need a paragraph I can read out loud. First the position, then the reason, then the numbers, and then the risk, said honestly, because the board trusts a risk that is named. And please send it by Wednesday at noon, so that I can read it twice.

When somebody asks you a hard question in a meeting, you need two answers ready, not one. The first is twenty seconds long: your position and your bottom line, nothing else. The second is about ninety seconds, and it has five parts: the position, the reason, the evidence, the caveat and the conclusion. Most people give a reason and then stop. They never get to the caveat, and the caveat is what makes the answer credible, because it shows that you have seen the problem and decided anyway. The small words matter here. Therefore takes the listener from the reason to the result. Although lets you admit a problem without losing your position. On the other hand tells them you are about to be fair to the other side. Without those words, the listener hears five separate sentences and has to connect them alone, and in a meeting nobody does that for you.

extra_audio.text: Start with your position. Then give the reason, and the result it leads to. Then give the evidence. Then admit the caveat, honestly. And finally, close with the bottom line.
